question: A 26-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes on insulin, who had a previous child with a neural tube defect, comes for preconception counselling. What is the appropriate folic acid dose to recommend?

answers.text: 400 micrograms (0.4 mg) daily, as recommended for all women planning pregnancy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: 400 mcg is the standard dose for low-risk women. This patient has two independent indications for high-dose: previous NTD-affected pregnancy and diabetes mellitus.

answers.text: 5 mg daily, because she has specific risk factors for NTD recurrence

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! High-dose folic acid 5 mg daily is indicated when there are risk factors for neural tube defects, including: prior NTD-affected pregnancy, diabetes mellitus, antiepileptic drug use, BMI >30, or family history of NTD. This patient has two such risk factors.

answers.text: 1 mg daily as a compromise between standard and high dose

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: 1 mg is not a recognised standard dose in preconception guidelines. The choice is between 0.4 mg (standard) and 5 mg (high-risk).

answers.text: No folic acid is needed because she already had a previous pregnancy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Folic acid is indicated in every pregnancy and is especially important here given the previous NTD and diabetes. Having had a previous pregnancy does not remove this need.

overallFeedback.feedback: High-dose folic acid 5 mg daily (not 400 mcg) is required when there are NTD risk factors such as previous NTD pregnancy, diabetes, antiepileptic drugs, or BMI >30.
Well done! High-dose folic acid (5 mg) is indicated for diabetes, previous NTD, antiepileptics, BMI >30, coeliac disease, and thalassaemia.
